findings.cited_line: - runs under the repository's pre-approved permission allowlists ONLY; the D9 skip list applies unchanged and no permissive flag exists that this mode accepts. IF a permission prompt would block the detached session THEN the run stalls until the governor's wall-clock timeout produces a clean stop at a slice boundary, recorded in the feed as state=escalated with the stall named as the reason (D-1).
findings.defect: The command promises that a permission-blocked detached session will be stopped by the governor timeout and write an escalation. scripts/autonomy/governor.sh is a synchronous check called once per slice attempt; it reads elapsed time only when invoked and exits. scripts/autonomy/launch-background-run.sh launches nohup without a timeout supervisor. A session blocked before its next call cannot run that check or update the feed. wos/autonomous-track.md and ADR-0081 repeat the promise but add no enforcement mechanism. This is an unsupported guarantee about the cited helper, not a missing helper path.
findings.proposed_fix: State that the governor checks timeout only when control returns between slices. Name manual intervention as the unblock for a permission-stalled session; require an independently enforced timeout before promising automatic stall-to-escalation in detached mode.
findings.family_sites: rg -n 'governor.s wall-clock timeout produces|stalls until' commands: autonomous-run.md:62 only. Matching doctrine: wos/autonomous-track.md, Background runs; docs/adr/0081-background-autonomous-run.md, decision 1. Helper verification: scripts/autonomy/governor.sh and scripts/autonomy/launch-background-run.sh; directory search over scripts found no supervisor wired to this launcher.

findings.cited_line: description: Run a short socratic intake that questions whether the stated problem is the right problem BEFORE a task exists, then write a task-level BRIEF.md (problem statement, success criteria, non-goals, recommended approach, named deliverables) that task-init consumes. Asks one question at a time and prefers multiple choice. Use when an objective is fuzzy, broad, or possibly mis-scoped and worth shaping before any task folder is created. Do not use when the objective is already specific enough to state in one sentence (run task-init directly), for a bug fix or hotfix (use incident-triage), when the gap is a decision inside an existing task (use decision-interview), or when the gap is missing facts (use targeted-questions).
findings.defect: The description routes a bug fix or hotfix to incident-triage even though this command runs before a task exists. Its own operating gate at line 49 and DoD at line 127 instead route that case to task-init. commands/incident-triage.md explicitly excludes runs with no active task folder, so the advertised route leads to an unmet precondition.
findings.proposed_fix: Change the frontmatter bug-fix and hotfix route to task-init, matching the existing operating gate and DoD; incident-triage can follow once the task exists.
findings.family_sites: rg -n 'for a bug fix or hotfix|objective is already clear or a hotfix|bug fix or hotfix' commands: problem-framing.md:3,49,127. Destination boundary verified in commands/incident-triage.md:3.

findings.cited_line: - **Game-design mode (gated, off by default; DECISIONS D-2, ADR-0069).** When invoked with `--game-design` (or when the objective is clearly a game in either dimension), keep the same five-field BRIEF.md but shape the socratic intake around game-design framing: the core gameplay loop (the repeated moment-to-moment action), the key mechanics, the win and lose conditions, the target platform (2D mobile by default), and an explicit scope boundary (the smallest playable slice). Field 5 (named deliverables) then names game artifacts (a playable scene, a mechanic, a level), and the recommended approach weighs a thin first-playable. This mode adds questions and brief content; it never alters the five-field structure or the terminal route. On a game brief the next command is still `task-init`, which then routes to `godot-scene-plan` for the scene architecture (Godot 2D-mobile cluster, ADR-0069). Without the flag (and a non-game objective) the intake is unchanged.
findings.defect: The game-mode rule covers games in either dimension without limiting the engine, but states that task-init then routes every game brief to godot-scene-plan. Current commands/task-init.md does not carry that scene-planning route. commands/implementation-plan.md:57 owns engine routing and selects unity-scene-plan for Unity and godot-scene-plan for Godot, per ADR-0132. The command therefore describes a stale downstream owner and a wrong destination for Unity briefs.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep task-init as the terminal route and replace the downstream claim with a pointer to implementation-plan's engine-specific scene-plan routing, or omit that downstream claim entirely.
findings.family_sites: rg -n 'then routes to `godot-scene-plan`' commands: problem-framing.md:56 only. Current route verified in commands/implementation-plan.md:57 and docs/adr/0132-unity-scene-plan-command.md, decision G-5; directory search of commands confirms task-init has no matching scene-plan routing rule.

findings.cited_line: - The output either returns a NO_OP routed to the right command for the case (`task-init` when the objective is already clear or a hotfix; `what-next` when an active task already exists, since a mid-task NO_OP routed to `task-init` would spawn a duplicate task) or contains a single next clarifying question; a batched wall of questions or a manufactured interview on an already-clear objective is invalid output.
findings.defect: This DoD permits only a NO_OP or a single next clarifying question. Required output item 2 at line 64 explicitly permits the assembled brief when framing is complete, and the next DoD bullet validates that completed brief. A completed, reviewed brief with no remaining question fails the first DoD bullet, encouraging an unnecessary additional question.
findings.proposed_fix: Add the completed five-field brief as the third allowed output state, alongside the routed NO_OP and the single next clarifying question.
findings.family_sites: rg -n 'or contains a single next clarifying question|assembled brief|When framing is complete' commands: problem-framing.md:64,127,128; site-unique completion-state mismatch.

findings.cited_line: description: Bootstrap a design system from a Figma file using MCP tools. Extracts token variables, identifies components, creates the directory structure, and generates scaffolded foundation docs and a component inventory. Use when starting a new project with a Figma design file. Do not use when the design system docs already exist or when there is no Figma file.
findings.defect: The frontmatter has negative triggers but names no sibling for either of them. In particular, an existing design-system inventory has a concrete refresh destination, inventory-snapshot, whose description and required inputs cover refreshing the Figma inventory. The Advertise-stage boundary tells the caller to avoid bootstrap but does not expose that existing continuation.
findings.proposed_fix: Add inventory-snapshot as the route when existing docs need an inventory refresh. Optionally name image-to-spec only for the separate case where no Figma source exists and the user has an image to document.
findings.family_sites: rg -n 'design system docs already exist|no Figma file|no Figma source' commands: design-bootstrap.md:3, inventory-snapshot.md:3, image-to-spec.md:3,20,116. Sibling inputs verified in commands/inventory-snapshot.md:36-40.

findings.cited_line: - `full`: `tables+rls` plus relevant functions, triggers, extensions, and server version metadata
findings.defect: Full depth promises relevant triggers, but the canonical DB_CONTEXT format at lines 77-114 has only metadata, extensions, tables, and functions, with no trigger field or section. Required output item 5 mandates that format, and the DoD enumerates evidence for other schema objects without triggers. An executor can follow the prescribed snapshot exactly while silently dropping a requested part of full depth. Searches over commands, wos, and docs/adr found no delegated trigger snapshot format.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a full-depth trigger section or per-table field to the canonical snapshot, recording the trigger name, table, timing and event, and invoked function from live introspection, with an explicit absent or unclear result where applicable. Apply the same correction to the Supabase sibling.
findings.family_sites: rg -n 'functions, triggers|## Triggers|### Triggers|Triggers \(only' commands wos docs/adr: full-depth promises in commands/db-context-postgres.md:50 and commands/db-context-supabase.md:48; neither canonical snapshot supplies a trigger field. wos/task-file-contracts.md:111-115 delegates DB_CONTEXT ownership to these commands rather than defining a missing trigger format.
